one_month_reasoning: Inside the window: Intel's Q3 2026 report, estimated by aggregators for Thu 2026-10-22 after the close (Intel has not confirmed the date; small chance it slips past Oct 31). Guide $15.8-16.8B revenue, ~42% non-GAAP GM, $0.38 EPS vs consensus ~$0.39 / $16.4B. Channel trackers and Intel's own confirmed Xeon/Core price hikes (Tom's Hardware), ~40% allocation fill and back-end-loaded supply make a beat and firm Q4 guide more likely than not. Against that: the stock rose 40%+ in September on narrative, 8 of the last 11 next-day earnings reactions were negative (supervisor's recomputation, mean absolute move ~11%), and the company's lock-up ends at the earlier of the Q3 release or ~Nov 8, so a fresh raise becomes possible right after the print. Net: median slightly below spot (~$118.5, P(>=120)=0.48) with ~21% one-month log-sigma (76%/3.5 plus an earnings move), lower tail a touch fatter than lognormal for post-run reversal/raise risk.

fair_value.method: Blend of 50% forward P/E (CY2028 EPS $2.90 x 33x = $96) and 50% SOTP (Products $17.5B after-tax x 22x = $385B + foundry option $117B + Mobileye/Altera $9.4B - net debt after H2 burn ~$3B - NCI $15.6B = ~$493B over 5.40B diluted shares = ~$91). Blended ~$94; the $120 price embeds more foundry success than external revenue ($293M in Q2) yet evidences.

inputs_detail.derivation: Consensus $2.06 with upward revision momentum; Q2-Q4 2026 run-rate already ~$0.40-0.43/qtr, plus 8-20% server CPU price hikes and sold-out supply per channel trackers -> ~$0.55-0.60/qtr through 2027. Intel itself confirmed list-price hikes on select Xeon/Core parts (Tom's Hardware), so the pricing tailwind is not only broker-sourced.

~25% growth on $2.30 as capacity adds (18A ramp; 14A risk production H2 2027 and HVM 2028 per Q2 call) and foundry losses narrow; below the $3.44 high estimate because foundry still loses ~$8B/yr (Ashton) and capex >$20B. Already on the post-offering diluted count (interest on $22.6B net proceeds offsets most of the ~5% dilution).

Premium to TSMC's ~23x 10-yr average and Nvidia ~28x (Fool) for supply-constrained growth plus foundry optionality; Ashton uses 22-25x for Products alone. 33x on consolidated EPS that is depressed by foundry losses.

bear.story: CPU shortage eases as AMD Venice/Arm capacity arrives and hyperscaler capex digests; Xeon hikes reverse, margins slip to high-30s; no binding 14A anchor by mid-2027 despite the internal H2 2027 risk-production milestone; a post-lock-up equity raise adds dilution. Rerates to ~25x $2.50.

base.story: Supply-constrained CPU cycle persists through 2027, EPS ~$2.3 CY27 / $2.9 CY28; 14A hits PDK 0.9 and internal risk production on schedule, one or two external 14A/18A-P commitments announced but small near-term revenue; multiple compresses from ~60x to ~40x CY28. Roughly flat.

bull.story: Apple M-series on 18A-P ships in 2027 and a large 14A anchor (Apple/Nvidia/Terafab) signs with prepayments ahead of 2028 HVM; agentic-AI CPU demand keeps EPS revisions rising (CY28 >$3.5); market values foundry as a TSMC alternative.

thesis_break_reason: Below ~$70 (about 25x my ~$2.8 Products-based EPS with little foundry value, 26% under the $95 August offering/CEO purchase price and well below the July 2026 low of $81.79) the market would be saying the CPU pricing/allocation cycle has broken or the 14A/Apple/Terafab customer pipeline has failed despite the on-schedule process milestones. That is more than ordinary 76%-vol noise from $120 over a few months.
